venue.name: Nanaimo Arts Council
venue.description: The Nanaimo Arts Council is a volunteer run charity made up of local artists and arts organisations in and around Nanaimo. It does not run a building of its own. Its work is connecting artists with the community through ArtWalk, an annual weekend festival in venues across downtown Nanaimo, a member exhibition in the Port Theatre lobby, three online galleries, and annual poetry and short fiction competitions published in its Sea Wolf magazine. Nothing on its site is a visit or a workshop a school or daycare group can book, and its only published address is a post office box.
venue.seasonal_notes: ArtWalk is the council's annual festival and its next run is listed on their calendar for November 2026. Their events calendar for the autumn is otherwise film screenings, a craft fair and a members' exhibition.

gaps: This is a different organisation from the Nanaimo Art Gallery on Commercial Street, which is catalogued separately. The arts council borrows the gallery's Art Lab for one of its events, which is easy to mix up.

Nothing bookable by a children's group is published. The council runs festivals, competitions, online galleries and a magazine, and it supports other arts organisations rather than hosting visits itself. If you want a session for a group, ask them who they would point you to.

No venue and no street address. Their only published address is a post office box, PO Box 401 Station A, Nanaimo BC V9R 5L3, so there is nowhere to put them on a map and no washrooms, lunch space or parking to describe.

The one thing on the site aimed at children is a free drop in art demonstration during the Commercial Street Night Market, run with Collage Club Nanaimo inside the Nanaimo Art Gallery's Art Lab. The activity takes 15 to 20 minutes, it is open to all ages, and the council calls it annual. The 2026 date has already passed and no new one is posted, so it is an event to watch for rather than something to book.

ArtWalk is free to walk around and there is a free hop on hop off shuttle between venues, but nothing on the page addresses groups, ages, supervision or a meeting point. If you were thinking of walking a class round it, ask them first.

No photographs of anything a group would see. The site's pictures are artwork from the online galleries, sponsor logos and one forest photograph used as a page background, so there is no header image for this record.
Whether the council would come to a classroom, or connect a group with one of its member artists, is not addressed anywhere on the site.
